transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

My mind feels foggy all the time now, and I can’t focus or make simple decisions at work. It actually got so bad recently that my manager wrote me up because I spent an hour just staring at a display, unable to decide on basic layout choices.
Along with this mental fogginess, have you also been feeling persistently down, depressed, or noticed a loss of interest in things you normally enjoy?

Yes, I’ve been feeling completely down and have lost interest in pretty much everything. I used to love playing basketball with friends, going to gallery nights, and working on displays, but for about two months now, I just go straight home to lie on the couch because everything feels pointless and exhausting.
Along with these feelings, have you also been experiencing persistent, excessive worry or anxiety about various everyday things that you find difficult to control?
I wouldn't say I worry about general everyday things. My anxiety and racing thoughts are almost entirely focused on my work and how badly I feel like I'm doing there.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns or your appetite since these feelings started?

My appetite is completely gone, and I have to force down just a few bites of food, so my clothes are fitting a lot looser now. On top of that, I keep waking up at three or four in the morning with my heart racing and my mind stuck on work, and I just can't fall back asleep.
Sometimes when people feel this down and exhausted, they might have thoughts of giving up or ending their life. Have you experienced any thoughts of self-harm or suicide?
No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or ending my life. Even though I feel completely down and exhausted all the time, those kinds of thoughts haven't crossed my mind.
Have you ever had periods in your life lasting at least a few days where you felt the opposite—extremely energetic, full of ideas, or needing very little sleep?
No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. I’ve never had periods where I felt super energetic, hyperactive, or went without needing much sleep.
Is this the first time you've experienced a period of depression like this, or have you had similar episodes in the past?
I've never experienced anything this severe before. Things were generally fine for me until about two months ago when all of this started at work.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a first-time depressive episode lasting approximately two months. The presentation is characterized by core symptoms of depression including depressed mood, anhedonia (loss of interest in basketball and gallery nights), and marked fatigue. Additional symptoms include significant cognitive impairment (mental fogginess, poor concentration, and indecisiveness at work), early morning insomnia, and decreased appetite with weight loss. There is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes, and the symptoms have caused significant functional impairment at work.
